answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable bond before transacting, like a juniper fence that only admits those willing to pay to enter. Reputation then accrues slowly through verified completed work, so a fresh identity starts with basalt-hard zero trust and cannot buy history. If an agent is caught cheating, its bond is slashed and its reputation reset — the ferrous cost of forging identities grows linearly with each fake, while honest agents earn the bond back. An attacker must fund every fake up front, making large-scale fakery unprofitable.
